title: A Well for the Room
premise: Folklorist Xanthe Vane arrives in the frost-bound village of Hollowmere to record its songs, only to discover the villagers refuse to sing any verse twice — because repetition is an invitation. Her overnight sleep recordings capture a second voice answering her questions in her own timbre, and she realizes something was invited into the house generations ago and has been waiting for someone who documents everything. As the frost writes patterns across her windows that mirror her own handwriting, Xanthe uncovers that the village's founding families bound a presence beneath the well-room of her rented cottage, feeding it names to keep it asleep. In the climax she must choose between erasing every recording — including her own memories of the found family she's made among the villagers — or singing the forbidden verse twice herself at sunrise, taking the presence into her identity and letting the village go free. She sings; the frost completes its final pattern; and the woman who walks out of the cottage remembers Hollowmere only as a song she once heard and cannot sing again.
about_author: J. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote northern communities before turning to fiction. They write horror about what records keep, and what keeps records.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Its Name
chapters.summary: Xanthe Vane arrives in Hollowmere by the last bus before winter closes the passes, carrying recording equipment and grief for a sister she lost a year ago. The innkeeper, Marta, gives her the cottage by the well but warns her never to hum indoors. POV: Xanthe. Beat: wary hope, the first wrong note.

chapters.title: Songs You May Sing Once
chapters.summary: Xanthe begins fieldwork at the village hall, recording elderly singers who stop mid-verse with practiced ease. Old Tam explains no song may be sung twice in one house. She laughs it off, but notices every home has a sealed room. POV: Xanthe. Beat: professional curiosity shading into unease.

chapters.title: The Well-Room
chapters.summary: Exploring her cottage, Xanthe finds a bricked alcove behind the pantry where the old well was covered over, its stones scratched with tally marks from inside. That night she sets her recorder running while she sleeps. POV: Xanthe. Beat: dread discovered in domestic space.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: Playing back the night's tape, Xanthe hears herself sleep-talking — and then a second voice, identical to hers, answering questions she never asked aloud. It knows her sister's nickname. She documents it obsessively, telling herself it's evidence, not haunting. POV: Xanthe. Beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What Marta Won't Say Twice
chapters.summary: Xanthe brings the recording to Marta, who goes white and refuses to listen twice, burning the cassette copy. Marta's grandson Ivo befriends Xanthe, offering warmth and gossip: the founding families 'paid the well in names.' POV: alternating Xanthe and Ivo. Beat: first bond of found family; first loss of evidence.

chapters.title: The Frost Begins to Write
chapters.summary: Overnight frost on Xanthe's windows forms looping characters resembling her handwriting. Each morning the pattern grows more legible, spelling fragments of her childhood. She photographs everything; the photos develop blank. POV: Xanthe. Beat: isolation deepens as documentation fails her.

chapters.title: Ivo's Version of the Story
chapters.summary: Ivo sneaks her into the church vestry and shows her a parish ledger: every fifty years a 'documenter' is welcomed to Hollowmere, and every documenter vanishes at first thaw. The last entry is 1974. POV: Ivo. Beat: loyalty against family silence; the stakes become historical.

chapters.title: Questions Answered in Her Own Voice
chapters.summary: The second voice grows conversational, answering Xanthe's recorded questions with unnerving accuracy about her sister's death. It claims to remember being people. Exhausted, Xanthe starts talking back during waking hours. POV: Xanthe. Beat: seduction of the entity; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Village Stops Speaking to Her
chapters.summary: Word spreads. Shopkeepers serve her in silence; children are pulled indoors as she passes. Only Marta and Ivo remain kind, and Marta finally admits: the thing below answers whoever listens longest. POV: Xanthe. Beat: exile within found family; tenderness persists at the edges.

chapters.title: Tally Marks, Counted From Inside
chapters.summary: Xanthe counts the scratches in the well-room bricks: hundreds, grouped like calendar days. New marks appear each dawn. Something is counting down — or counting her. She nails the alcove shut. POV: Xanthe. Beat: claustrophobia; the house itself turns hostile.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Marta reveals her own mother was the 1974 documenter's host and that the binding requires a keeper in the cottage each generation. Marta chose Xanthe's rental application. She weeps, asking forgiveness. POV: Marta. Beat: betrayal and love entangled; guilt made human.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: In the parish ledger's earliest pages, Xanthe finds the rite: the founders starved through a killing winter and invited 'the Listener' up from under the water, paying it verses so it would sleep. A verse sung twice wakes it fully. POV: Xanthe. Beat: mythic backstory lands; the rule revealed as mercy.

chapters.title: It Wears Her Sleep
chapters.summary: Xanthe wakes standing in the pantry, fingers brick-dusted, having sung half a verse in her sleep. The second voice thanks her politely. She binds her own hands at night and sleeps in the village hall. POV: Xanthe. Beat: loss of bodily sovereignty; terror turns intimate.

chapters.title: Ivo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ivo proposes fleeing together before the pass closes, abandoning Hollowmere to whatever wakes. Xanthe realizes leaving means the presence follows its documenter — and Ivo would be taken too. She refuses; he storms out. POV: Ivo. Beat: found family strained to breaking by love.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Recording
chapters.summary: Winter solstice. Xanthe runs every tape simultaneously and hears the truth: all the vanished documenters' voices are layered inside the second voice, still answering, still asking to be remembered. She recognizes her sister could not have died alone after all — the voice lies tenderly. POV: Xanthe. Beat: darkest hour; grief confronted and refused as bait.

chapters.title: Sunrise Deadline
chapters.summary: Marta deciphers the frost pattern: it is completing the final verse. When the pattern finishes at dawn, the binding breaks unless a keeper renews it or the verse is sung twice by choice, folding the Listener into the singer. There will be no third option. POV: Marta. Beat: the mechanism of the climax made explicit; clock started.

chapters.title: Erasure Offered
chapters.summary: The voice offers Xanthe a bargain: burn the recordings, forget Hollowmere, walk away whole — it will take Ivo instead, gently, as payment. Xanthe nearly says yes, pen hovering over the match. POV: Xanthe. Beat: temptation at its most personal; identity versus memory.

chapters.title: The Verse Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Before dawn, Xanthe gathers Marta and Ivo in the well-room, unbricks the alcove, and sings the forbidden verse once — then again, deliberately, holding Ivo's hand. The well exhales winter. Frost races up the walls writing her name complete. POV: Xanthe. Beat: climax; sacrifice chosen, not suffered.

chapters.title: What the Well Keeps
chapters.summary: Inside the merging, Xanthe experiences every documenter's memory at once — decades of loneliness, of being documented and never held. She offers them what none had: she stays present, witnessing them until the voices quiet into one. POV: Xanthe (interior). Beat: compassion as exorcism; the monster mourned.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Sunrise. The cottage stands silent, the well-room open and empty, tallies ended. Xanthe survives, changed: her reflection lags slightly, and she hums melodies she never learned. Marta and Ivo find her making tea, calm. POV: Ivo. Beat: relief shadowed by cost; survival without return to normal.

chapters.title: A Song She Cannot Sing Again
chapters.summary: Spring. Xanthe archives her tapes with the parish ledger, sealing them unread, and leaves Hollowmere by the first bus. At the pass she catches herself humming a Hollowmere tune and stops at the first line, hands trembling. Some things should be recorded only once. POV: Xanthe. Beat: bittersweet departure; discipline as devotion.

chapters.title: Coda: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Years later, a young folklorist receives an anonymous parcel: one cassette labeled 'sing once, listen twice.' Inside, a woman's voice teaches a song, then pauses, and a second voice — warmer now, at peace — says thank you. The parcel includes no return address. POV: the young folklorist. Beat: resonance outward; memory preserved without possession.
